body: Pursuit Force is Bigbig Studios' PSP action game, first released in Australia on 10 November 2005. An elite police officer confronts the gangs of Capital State through missions that mix driving, shooting and spectacular vehicle changes. The defining action is a leap from one speeding vehicle to another, allowing the officer to fight its occupants and take control. A car is therefore a temporary position within the chase rather than the object that must always survive it. The next useful vehicle may be the one currently trying to escape.

Driving positions the officer for an attack, while shooting clears the destination vehicle before it can be commandeered. That relationship makes the chase a sequence of changing platforms, with each successful leap renewing the options available. Thirty missions also include boats, on-foot encounters and helicopter gunfire. Performance ratings unlock additional content, and progress grants abilities that help with later confrontations. The player has to balance speed and survival with the need to approach a target closely enough to change the situation, turning proximity into an opportunity rather than merely a collision risk.

Richard Jacques composed the score for a campaign organised around five gangs, each offering six missions. Race and time-trial modes provide separate driving challenges after the story's more elaborate set pieces. Reviews were positive, and Bigbig followed the game with Pursuit Force: Extreme Justice in 2007. The original's strongest idea is immediately understandable in motion: the hero can leave the car while the chase continues. That single stunt gives the PSP game a recognisable identity and lets driving and third-person shooting operate as parts of the same continuous action sequence.
